hooks.text: Captain Fetterman rode over a ridge and vanished with eighty men.
Why did eighty soldiers vanish behind a single Wyoming ridge?
Eighty-one men crossed a ridge in 1866 and none ever returned.

title: Why Did 80 Soldiers Vanish at the Fetterman Fight? 🤯
description: In 1866, an arrogant commander led eighty men into a trap that would become the U.S. Army's worst Plains defeat until Little Bighorn.

beats.text: Captain Fetterman rode over a ridge and vanished with eighty men.
beats.visual: portrait of Captain William J. Fetterman, photograph, 1860s

beats.text: In 1866, his commander ordered him never to cross that crest.
beats.visual: portrait of Colonel Henry B. Carrington, photograph, 1866

beats.text: A relief party arrived to find no one left alive.
beats.visual: photograph of the Fetterman Massacre Monument at Massacre Hill, 1908

beats.text: They realized Native decoys had lured the command into an ambush.
beats.visual: sketch of Lakota warrior Crazy Horse, drawing, 19th century

beats.text: Fetterman reportedly boasted eighty men could conquer the Sioux nation.
beats.visual: woodcut of Fort Phil Kearny stockade, drawing, 1866

beats.text: No survivor returned to explain why he rode over that ridge.

better_than_last: Used a 'mystery' structure to create suspense by withholding the commander's hubristic quote until the end.
